sections.label: Task 1
sections.title: Task 1 — Household recycling in three English cities
sections.instructions: You should spend about 20 minutes on this task. Write at least 150 words. You should write your answer in the box below.

questionGroups.instructions: You should spend about 20 minutes on this task. Write at least 150 words. You should write your answer in the box below.

questions.prompt:
The table below shows the amount of household waste that was recycled in three English cities in 2000, 2005 and 2010, measured in tonnes per household per year. In 2000, Manchester recorded 0.9 tonnes, Leeds 1.1 and York 1.8; in 2005 the figures were 1.4, 1.5 and 1.9 respectively, and by 2010 they stood at 2.2, 1.3 and 2.0.

Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.
questions.explanation: What a Band 8 answer does here: (1) one overview sentence — over the decade all three cities rose, but Manchester grew fastest while York's increase was modest; (2) a body paragraph per city with specific figures and comparisons — Manchester more than doubled (0.9 to 2.2) and ended above York, which started highest, while Leeds peaked in 2005 (1.5) before slipping to 1.3; (3) precise comparison language — "more than double", "the slowest rise", "edged up to"; (4) paraphrasing the table instead of copying the title sentence. No opinions, no causes, and at least 150 words — a missing overview is the most common reason this task scores 6.

sections.label: Task 2
sections.title: Task 2 — Punishments and road safety
sections.instructions: You should spend about 40 minutes on this task. Write at least 250 words. Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience.

questionGroups.instructions: You should spend about 40 minutes on this task. Write at least 250 words. Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience.

questions.prompt:
Some people believe that the best way to improve road safety is to increase the severity of punishments for drivers who break the rules, such as heavy fines and longer prison sentences. Others argue that there are more effective measures to reduce the number of road accidents.

Discuss both these views and give your own opinion.
questions.explanation: What a Band 8 answer does here: (1) an introduction that paraphrases both views and states a clear position — penalties help, but prevention is stronger; (2) one paragraph per view, each with a reason plus a developed example — harsher fines and licence loss deter reckless drivers, while better road design, driver training and enforcement cameras stop accidents before they happen; (3) the opinion stated early, developed and repeated in the conclusion — not left as a surprise; (4) varied cohesion ("whereas", "in my view") rather than a mechanical "Firstly/Secondly"; (5) accurate less-common vocabulary: deterrent, reckless driving, enforcement, infrastructure. Discussing both views without taking a side is the classic 6.5 pattern.
